title: rulings_check gates at exit 1 on findings while the runner documents the five register checks as report-only and reports exit 2
body:
`bin/.devbin/cmd/precommit:340-352` states the contract for the five register checks in as many words:

> All five are REPORT-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: each exits 0 whether it is clean or has findings, and non-zero ONLY when it cannot measure at all. So a refusal from any of the five is never "the register is wrong" -- it is "this instrument could not answer", which is a broken instrument.

**`rulings_check.sh` does not honour that contract.** Its last two arms are:

    if [ "$BAD" -gt 0 ]; then      ... ; exit 1; fi    # non-conforming declaration
    if [ "$DANGLING" -gt 0 ]; then       exit 1; fi    # a record that leads nowhere

Both are FINDINGS -- the check measured successfully and found something wrong -- and both gate. Its `die()` at line 104 is the genuine cannot-measure path and it is `exit 2`, so the file distinguishes the two cases internally and then gates on both.

**And the runner's failure message names the code the instrument did not emit:**

    rulings_check.sh -- could not measure ratification provenance (exit 2; its findings never gate)

printed when the instrument exited **1**, on a finding, having measured fine. Every clause of that line is wrong for the case that produced it: it did measure, the code was not 2, and the finding did gate.

## Measured

In an isolated clone, an unstaged edit changing one `target.rulings` record to `issue 9999`: `rulings_check` rc=**1**, and its report prints `DANGLING -- a record is declared and leads nowhere (1)`. Control: clean clone rc=0. Siblings on the same mutation: `corrected_check` rc=0, `class_vocab_check` rc=0.

## Why this is 0093's shape, and the correction that comes with it

0093 is an arm reporting a code nothing reads while sitting inside the branch that acts on it. This is that, one level up: the RUNNER's message describes a contract the instrument does not keep, and the operator reads the message rather than the source.

**vc raised this class against `corrected_check` and I told them there was nothing to file. That was right about `corrected_check` -- it exits 2 on a genuine inability to measure and the runner blocking on it is the correct polarity, because a green from an instrument that did not run is worth nothing -- and it was wrong about the family.** vc's sighting was correct and its instance was not, which is the estate's own "a correct sighting with a wrong explanation" class; my dismissal inherited the wrong instance instead of checking the other four.

## What is NOT decided here

Whether the defect is the instrument or the description. A citation that leads nowhere is arguably worth blocking on -- in which case `rulings_check` is right, the runner's comment is too broad, and its message needs rewriting. Or the five really are report-only, and `rulings_check` should print `DANGLING` and exit 0 like its siblings. **Picking one is a contract decision about what the gate is for, not an implementation detail, and it is not cc's to make.** Both fixes are XS once ruled.
